# Copilot instructions — `MHTaleb/gaming` monorepo

This repository hosts several independent indie projects. **Each project has its own rules.**
Do not apply one project's conventions to another.

## Projects

| Folder | Project | Stack | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `glad-to-see-you/` | **Glad to See You** — 3D dark-fantasy mobile action game | Unity 6.3 LTS, URP, C# | **This file (sections below) + `glad-to-see-you/AGENTS.md`** — read both before working there |
| `packet-defense/`, `neon-stack/` | web games (vanilla JS, Capacitor) | zero-dependency, no build step | see `.github/instructions/runtime-zero.instructions.md`-style per-project files if present |
| `runtime-zero/` | Godot RPG | Godot 4.x, GDScript | `.github/instructions/runtime-zero.instructions.md` |
| `deploy/` | staging deploy tooling for the web games | bash/systemd/nginx | see `deploy/README.md` |

**When working inside `glad-to-see-you/`, the following rules apply.**

## The project

A serious, visually impressive **3D mobile dark-fantasy action game** (vertical slice):
one hero, one arena, third-person combat, premium presentation on mobile budgets.
Engine: **Unity 6000.3.24f1 (Unity 6.3 LTS)**. Render pipeline: **URP** (mobile-appropriate, not HDRP).
Platform: **Android first, iOS-compatible architecture.**

## Required behavior

- Read `glad-to-see-you/AGENTS.md` and `Documentation/ARCHITECTURE.md` **before generating code**.
- **Never generate systems without first inspecting the existing architecture** — extend, don't duplicate.
- **Never create giant MonoBehaviour classes.** Composition; each script one clear responsibility.
- **Never introduce packages** (UPM or managed DLLs) **without explaining why** in the response/commit.
- **Never silently change architectural conventions** (namespaces `GladToSeeYou.*`, asmdef layout,
  ScriptableObject data flow, EventBus usage, folder structure).
- **Never put secrets** (API keys, credentials) in code, scenes, or committed configs. Use `.env` (gitignored).
- **Never generate desktop-only graphics systems** for this mobile project. Every:
  render feature, shadow technique, post effect, particle rate, texture resolution —
  must be defensible against `Documentation/PERFORMANCE_BUDGET.md`.
- **Never fabricate asset filenames** or pretend assets were created. With art tasks, use the MCP tooling
  (Unity/Blender/Meshy) or create clearly-marked procedural placeholders.
- **Mobile-first thinking**: prefer batching/instancing-friendly setups, bake where possible,
  keep real-time shadow casters few, treat GC allocations in Update as bugs.
- **Deterministic bootstrap**: the vertical slice is generated by `VerticalSliceFactory` (code), so scenes
  are reproducible. Prefer fixing/extending that factory over hand-editing scene files.

## MCP tools available (configured in `.vscode/mcp.json`)

- **unity-mcp** (MCP for Unity v10.2.0): inspect/control the Unity editor, read the console, run tests,
  manage scenes/assets. Requires the Unity package installed in-editor + editor running.
- **blender-mcp** (mcp-for-blender v2.0.4): drive Blender for mesh cleanup, LODs, materials, exports.
  Requires Blender running with the addon server started.
- **meshy** (official Meshy MCP): text/image-to-3D, remesh, rig, animate. **Paid credits —
  only use with explicit owner approval.**

## Verification expectations (for any generated change)

1. It compiles in Unity (state if you could not verify — never imply you did).
2. EditMode tests pass; add coverage for new logic.
3. Console is clean in play mode for the touched system.
4. For per-frame changes: a sentence on cost + where it was measured.
5. Docs updated when conventions/behavior change.

## Style

- C#: `GladToSeeYou.*` namespaces; `[SerializeField] private` references; no public mutable statics
  (the EventBus and service registry on `GameRoot` are the sanctioned exceptions); XML-doc public APIs.
- Prefer `TryGetComponent`, non-alloc physics queries, and cached property IDs / `Shader.PropertyToID`.
- Naming: gameplay data in ScriptableObjects (`*Data.cs`, `*Stats.cs`); services `*Service.cs`;
  MonoBehaviours named for what they own (`PlayerMovement`, `EnemyBrain`, `ThirdPersonCameraRig`).
